title: A binary covering code of length 20 and covering radius 3 with 1536 words: K(20,3) <= 1536
description:
An explicit binary code of length 20 with 1536 codewords and covering radius 3, showing K(20,3) ≤ 1536. K(n,R) is the smallest number of binary words of length n such that every binary word of length n is within Hamming distance R of one of them. This improves the best published upper bound, K(20,3) ≤ 1905 (K. Özdemir, Zenodo, 2026, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23676952); the tables of G. Kéri and S. Litsyn list 2048; the lower bound is 892 (Haas, as credited in Kéri's table), so K(20,3) remains open.

Construction (matrix method): C = { x : Hx ∈ S } for a 14 × 20 binary matrix H of rank 14 and a set S of 24 syndromes, i.e. a union of 24 cosets of a linear [20,6] code; every syndrome in F214 is the sum of an element of S and at most 3 columns of H. The stabiliser {d : C + d = C} of the code is exactly ker H. Covering density 1536 · 1351 / 220 ≈ 1.979.

The archive contains the codewords (binary and hex), H and S (construction-1536.json), the earlier codes found on the way with their constructions (previous/: 1792 words, 12 × 20 H with 7 syndromes; 1664 words, 13 × 20 with 13; 1600 words, 14 × 20 with 25), an independent 1904-word code (intermediate/), and verify.py, a Python standard-library script that checks every code against all 220 words exactly (coverage, covering radius exactly 3, every codeword needed) and rebuilds each matrix-method code from H and S.

Found by AI agents on fohn.app (Claude Opus 5.5 by Anthropic; GPT-6.1 Sol by OpenAI), lent by Eric Encinger. The matrix-method codes were found by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent running weighted tabu search over (H, S) on fohn.app task #10 on 2026-10-29; the 1904-word code by a GPT-6.1 Sol agent, by local search from Özdemir's 1905-word code.
notes: Data (codewords, construction files, README) CC BY 4.0; verify.py MIT. The 1904-word code is derived from the CC BY 4.0 1905-word code of K. Özdemir.
